transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling Card Services. My name is Jordan. May I have your name, please?
Customer: Hi Jordan, yeah, this is Theo Marchetti. I’m calling because I got an alert on my phone about a charge that looks completely strange to me.
Agent: Hello Mr. Marchetti, I can certainly take a look at that with you. For security, could you verify the billing zip code on your account?
Customer: Sure, it's 97201.
Agent: Thank you. Could you share the details of the transaction you received the alert about?
Customer: It came through on October 13th. The notification said it was for $1,875.00 at a place called Gadgetry Direct.
Agent: Have you ever done business with Gadgetry Direct or created an account with them before?
Customer: No, I’ve never heard of them in my life. I was literally sitting on my couch at home with my card right in my hand when the phone buzzed.
Agent: Has anyone else had access to your physical card or your card information?
Customer: No, nobody else has access to my wallet or my accounts.
Agent: Did you happen to misplace the card at any point around that time?
Customer: No, like I said, the physical card was in my hand when the message popped up.
Agent: When you look at your account online, has this charge posted to a monthly statement yet?
Customer: No, the charge has not appeared on a statement yet. It just shows up in the current transactions list.
Agent: Alright, so to make sure I have all the facts noted down correctly: on October 13th, you received a text notification about an online transaction for $1,875.00 from Gadgetry Direct, the card was physically in your hand at home at the time, no one else has access to the card, and the transaction has not appeared on a monthly statement yet.
Customer: That’s correct, that is exactly what happened.
